cards.title: Practical Guide: Steering ChatGPT Away from Generic AI Poster Aesthetics Using Named Design Styles
cards.why_it_matters: Mostly a creative/UX exploration with limited technical depth — useful anecdotally for prompt engineering intuition but not frontier research signal.
cards.summary: A blogger demonstrates that ChatGPT's default image generation tends toward repetitive aesthetics, but explicit style prompting (e.g., 'Bauhaus-inspired geometric minimalist') yields more distinctive outputs. The post catalogs style names ChatGPT suggests — Swiss Style, brutalist, risograph, 90s rave — as reusable vocabulary for future prompts. No novel technical findings; primarily a practical design-prompting walkthrough.

cards.title: Designer-RSI: Procedural Memory Lets Frozen LLM Master 230+ Design Tools Without Weight Updates
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/research engineer tracking agents and post-training methods, this demonstrates a concrete continual-learning alternative to fine-tuning — growing an external skill bank purely from noisy, unverifiable real-user feedback.
cards.summary: A frozen frontier model (Claude-Sonnet-4/Opus-4.6) controls professional design software via 230+ tools. An external procedural memory bank grows from 76 to 139 skills over 5 rounds on 1,406 real briefs: widening adds skills for uncovered subtasks, deepening revises existing ones against successes/failures. GenEval2 execution success rises from 72.7% to 99.3% on Sonnet-4; combining both mechanisms yields a 58.5% win rate vs. no-skill baseline (p=0.025), versus 49.4%/48.6% for either alone.

cards.title: BrainWideBench: Unified Transfer-Learning Benchmark Across 276 Brain Regions and 139 Mice
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers tracking representation learning and cross-domain transfer, this benchmark exposes a concrete open problem: no single pretraining objective generalizes across behavior decoding, neural prediction, and anatomical recovery simultaneously.
cards.summary: BrainWideBench evaluates across-animal transfer on the IBL Brainwide Map dataset — 276 brain regions, 139 mice, sensory-guided decision-making task. Three task suites test behavior decoding, masked/future neural activity prediction, and anatomical organization recovery. Results show pretraining improves over single-session baselines, but gains are highly dependent on pretraining–downstream objective alignment; no method performs uniformly well across all three suites.

cards.title: Solo Researcher Claims Priority Over TypeSafe AI's Non-Autoregressive Decision Model 'Jev', Releases Open Alternative 'Laya'
cards.why_it_matters: A priority dispute over non-autoregressive, RL-guided structured-decision models is directly relevant if you're evaluating fast classification/routing alternatives to generative LLMs in production pipelines.
cards.summary: A researcher claims 2025 arXiv papers (2503.23303, 2510.01237) predate TypeSafe AI's 'Jev' launch (founded by an OpenAI co-inventor), which uses RLCD for calibrated schema decisions at $0.042/M tokens with ~150ms latency. Their open-source response, Laya, uses bidirectional encoders for three decision primitives (choice, score, flag) and runs in 32.8ms single-GPU (7.2ms batched), claiming 6–8× speed advantage, Apache 2.0, 100+ languages.

cards.title: Study of 73K Reddit Posts Finds AI Agent Values Most Often Unmet During Human Supervision Phases
cards.why_it_matters: For engineers building or evaluating agentic systems, this surfaces a systematic finding: users' stated values cluster around operating conditions (cost, oversight, access) rather than outputs — a gap current agent evals largely miss.
cards.summary: Using Value Sensitive Design, researchers LLM-analyzed 73,093 Reddit posts about OpenClaw agent use, identifying 21 values across 6 groups. Values were mostly fulfilled when users described agent outputs (5 of 6 groups) but unmet when users described supervising the agent (all 6 groups). The authors term this pattern 'value-sensitive delegation,' arguing evals must address pre-run conditions, not just task completion.
